title: Prime-to-ell uniformization in standard form
statement: Let $X$ be an integral Noetherian scheme [def-pc-integral-scheme, def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] whose affine coordinate rings are quasi-excellent [def-exc-excellent-ring], let $\ell$ be a prime invertible on $X$, and let $U\subseteq X$ be a dense open subscheme [def-weil-open-immersion]. There exist an integral scheme $X'$, a proper morphism $p:X'\to X$ inducing an isomorphism over a dense open of $X$, a finite family of separated etale morphisms $e_i:E_i\to X'$ of finite type, finite locally free surjective morphisms $a_i:W_i\to E_i$ of constant positive ranks $r_i$ prime to $\ell$, finitely many regular Noetherian schemes $Y_b$, and $X$-morphisms $W_i\to Y=\coprod_bY_b$. The schemes $X',E_i,W_i,Y_b$ are of finite type over $X$. The family $(e_i)$ is completely decomposed: for every $x'\in X'$ there are $i$ and $z\in E_i$ over $x'$ with $\kappa(x')\to\kappa(z)$ an isomorphism. For every $b$, the inverse image $U\times_XY_b$ is the complement of a strict normal crossings boundary [def-trf-strict-normal-crossings-boundary] in $Y_b$. Proper, finite and flat have the meanings of [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions, def-weil-finite-integral-morphism, def-weil-flat-morphism], etale that of [def-weil-etale-morphism], and regular that of [def-weil-regular-scheme].

proof.text: Put $Z=X\setminus U$. This is closed since $U$ is open and nowhere dense since $U$ is dense. The hypotheses already give that $X$ is reduced, Noetherian and quasi-excellent, and that $\ell$ is invertible on $X$. Thus $(X,Z,\ell)$ satisfies the input hypotheses of the regular-cover theorem.

source.place: XIII 3.2.1: apply IX 1.1 to the complement of the dense open.

proof.text: Apply [lem-per-gabber-prime-to-ell-regular-cover] to $(X,Z,\ell)$. Obtain a finite $\ell'$-alteration covering family $q_b:Y_b\to X$, with each $Y_b$ regular and Noetherian and each $q_b$ of finite type, and strict normal crossings boundaries $H_b$ satisfying $|H_b|=q_b^{-1}(Z)$. Consequently the inverse image $U\times_XY_b$ is exactly the open complement $Y_b\setminus |H_b|$. We retain these $Y_b$; no later refinement is required to preserve a boundary on its own source.

source.place: IX Theorem 1.1; XIII 3.2.1, regular schemes Y_j and inverse images of U.

proof.text: Apply [lem-per-alteration-cover-standard-refinement] to this finite covering family in $\operatorname{alt}/X$. The scheme $X$ is integral and quasi-excellent, as required; $\ell$ is the same invertible prime. It gives $p:X'\to X$, the finite completely decomposed family $e_i:E_i\to X'$, the finite locally free surjections $a_i:W_i\to E_i$ of positive constant ranks prime to $\ell$, and $X$-morphisms $h_i:W_i\to Y_{b(i)}$. The conclusion of that theorem includes the dense-open isomorphism for $p$, integrality of $X'$, separatedness and finite type of the $e_i$, all the finite type assertions, and $q_{b(i)}h_i=pe_ia_i$.

source.place: II Theorem 3.2.3 and Corollary 2.2.4, as combined in XIII 3.2.1.

proof.text: Let $Y=\coprod_bY_b$ be the disjoint union scheme: its space is the disjoint union of the spaces of the $Y_b$, with the structure sheaf equal to theirs on each open and closed summand. Give it the $X$-map whose restriction to $Y_b$ is $q_b$. For every $i$, compose $h_i$ with the inclusion $Y_{b(i)}\hookrightarrow Y$. This is an $X$-morphism because its composite to $X$ is $q_{b(i)}h_i=pe_ia_i$. These are the requested maps $W_i\to Y$. Together with the boundary complements from Step 2 and the standard diagram from Step 3 they give every clause of the statement.

source.place: XIII 3.2.1, the top arrow to the finite disjoint union Y.

proof_origin.place: XIII 3.2.1, using IX Theorem 1.1 and II Theorem 3.2.3.
